summary: Tenant reporting accuracy delta and cost surge after enabling mixed-precision + prefix prefetch; request safe unwind assistance
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Greenline Health reports a sudden drop in model quality (increased hallucinations and lower BLEU/ROUGE on validation prompts) and an associated 2.4x increase in avg token cost after a staged enablement of a mixed-precision (8-bit) quant profile together with aggressive prefix-KV prefetching on their dedicated pool. They asked for an immediate safe unwind plan that minimizes user-visible downtime and cost exposure.

Impact:
- Business impact: Several clinician-facing flows returned lower-quality summaries leading to customer complaints and possible clinical risk.
- Scope: ~12% of requests routed to the optimized pool show quality regression; bucketed by tenant_id: greenline-prod (single-tenant dedicated pool).
- Cost: token spend on pool doubled for the last 6 hours.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity: greenline-prod-dedicated-us-east-1
- Runtime version: rwinf-2.8.1
- Optimization flags: quant_profile=mixed-8bit-fast, kv_prefetch=true, async_batching=true, batch_target_tokens=4096
- Deployed at: 2026-03-05T02:10:00Z (automated staged rollout)

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send a standard set of validation prompts to model redwood/gpt-13b-8bit pinned on greenline-prod tenant.
2) Observe generation quality and token counts.
3) Compare against the prior snapshot (pre-change) - customer attached metric deltas.

Observed telemetry & logs:
- Trace IDs (examples): trace-8f4c, trace-b7d2 (included in attachments).
- Console metrics: 95th latency stable, but per-token compute utilization increased and cost-per-response doubled.
- Eval metrics: validation BLEU dropped 9 points on summary suite; hallucination rate increased from 2.1% to 6.8%.
- Error logs: no obvious 5xx spike; no OOMs. Scheduler logs show larger avg batch sizes and more KV eviction churn.

Attachments:
- Customer-provided diffs and CSVs (attached to issue).
- Snapshot ID: snap.greenline.2026-03-05T01:50Z

Customer ask:
- Immediate safe unwinding of the optimization changes with minimal disruption, and guidance to re-run a conservative opt profile that preserves cost benefits without quality regressions.

2026-03-05 10:40 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Executed 10% traffic split rollback to snapshot snap.greenline.2026-03-05T01:50Z. Observed improvement in sample quality within 15 minutes on split traffic. Recorded metric diffs and attached graphs.

2026-03-05 12:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Notified customer and recommended next steps: expand rollback to 50% if stable and concurrently create a conservative optimizer profile. Customer requested full unwind if 50% shows improvement.

2026-03-06 02:15 - Engineering (Runtime): Investigating KV eviction and quantization interactions. Hypothesis: mixed-8bit-fast uses aggressive approximation kernels that amplify generation noise when combined with prefetch eviction patterns under this workload. No code changes deployed.

2026-03-07 05:50 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Per-customer planned full unwind completed (50% -> 100%) via config revert; customer reports restored metrics and reduced token cost. Drafting resolution notes and follow-ups.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Combined effect of mixed-precision kernels and aggressive kv_prefetch produced inconsistent attention weights on longer contexts leading to hallucination increase.

Hypothesis 2: Prefetch eviction churn caused increased recomputation overhead that inflated cost; async_batching with high batch_target_tokens amplified kernel quant error under certain sequence distributions.
Telemetry: 10% rollback test produced BLEU +6 points on split traffic and decreased token compute by ~38% for that slice. No infra-level errors found (no OOMs, no GPU driver faults).
Config audit: Customer had custom tenant override that set batch_target_tokens higher than recommended for mixed-8bit-fast; this override was not covered by the staged rollout guardrails.
resolution: Executed staged unwind for Greenline Health: 10% traffic split rollback to snapshot -> monitor -> expanded to 50% -> expanded to 100% once metrics improved. Reverted optimizer flags to conservative profile: quant_profile=8bit-safe (lower approximation), kv_prefetch=adaptive (LRU backpressure), batch_target_tokens=2048, async_batching=on with conservative thresholds. Restored snapshot snap.greenline.2026-03-05T01:50Z to tenant config store. Follow-up items: (1) Engineering to add a preflight check that blocks mixed-precision + high batch_target_tokens for tenants with long-context distributions; (2) Recommend customer run a smoke eval suite before next staged rollout; (3) Create a per-tenant optimizer-snapshot and a one-click revert button in console (tracked in INT-4021). Customer reported quality restored and token spend returned to baseline within two hours of full unwind.
